A codec is a mechanism or process for encoding/decoding data. An algorithm is a computational procedure. These are different categories — a codec IMPLEMENTS algorithms but is not itself an algorithm type. INSTANCE_OF is the wrong relation. This is a copula confusion: 'codec is an algorithm' is too broad and ignores the structural difference.

Buffer-size is a quantitative parameter — a number specifying capacity. It is not itself a measurement technique or process. INSTANCE_OF is wrong. Buffer-size quantifies a property of a buffer but is not a measurement of anything itself.

Frequency-weighting is a correction technique — it applies standardized curves to acoustic measurements (e.g., A-weighting). It is not itself a measurement. It modifies measurements; it does not constitute one. INSTANCE_OF is wrong.

Frequency is a fundamental physical concept — it is a property/parameter that pitch estimation operates ON, not something pitch estimation depends on operationally. Remove the concept of frequency from the taxonomy and pitch estimation as a technique for determining fundamental frequency would still have a well-defined operating principle. This is 'operates on' not 'depends on per Law 8b'.
